newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu to meet Palestinians on Hebron deal.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu to meet Palestinians on Hebron deal.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu plans to meet Palestinian negotiators on Friday to try to complete a deal on a long-overdue Israeli army redeployment in Hebron, officials on both sides said.

Palestinian negotiator Hassan Asfour said Netanyahu was due to meet security officials of the Palestinian delegation to discuss security arrangements in the volatile West Bank city. He declined to elaborate.
Israeli officials confirmed that Netanyahu planned to meet Palestinian negotiators on Friday but did give any details.

In Hebron, three petrol bombs were thrown at an Israeli army observation post opposite a building which houses Jewish settlers. Witnesses said the petrol bombs landed in a courtyard and that no one was hurt.

It was the latest in a series of attacks in Hebron since Israel and the PLO broke a three-month deadlock that kept the two sides from reaching an agreement on the handover of 80 percent of the city to Palestinian rule.
The incident occurred shortly after Netanyahu aide and key negotiator Yitzhak Molcho toured the city, home to about 400 Jewish settlers and more than 100,000 Palestinians.
Witnesses said Israeli soldiers rounded up and later released about two dozen Palestinians who were in the area. They said the soldiers smelled the men's hands for signs of petrol.
Jewish settlers began throwing rubbish from their enclave at Palestinians after the petrol bombs were thrown. Witnesses said Israeli troops quickly intervened to stop them.
In Amman, a spokesman for the Palestinian Islamic militant group Hamas denounced the imminent accord as a sellout that would legitimise Hebron's partition between Jews and Arabs.

"Hamas movement calls on the Palestinian people generally and the herioc people of Hebron in particular to reject and resist such plots," Ibrahim Ghosheh, an official spokesman for Hamas in Jordan, told Reuters.

Hebron is the last of seven West Bank cities occupied since the 1967 Middle East war that Israel agreed to turn over to the Palestinian Authority under a 1995 self-rule deal signed by the previous Labour-led government.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat told Palestinian lawmakers at a closed session on Thursday that he expected the Hebron accord to be ready for signing by December 30 or 31, the deputies said.
Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai on Thursday met Palestinian and Israeli negotiators to help them phrase some of the clauses in the deal, said a Defence Ministry statement.
The statement also said that Mordechai met U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk, who along with U.S. Consul General Edward Abington have been following the negotiations.

Earlier this week Israeli and PLO negotiators, nudged by U.S. special envoy to the Middle East Dennis Ross, broke the logjam that blocked a deal, leading to a meeting between Netanyahu and Arafat on Tuesday.
Palestinian negotiators said that the breakthrough came when Israel agreed to adhere to the original text of the deal.
Israeli officials say the accord now being drafted provides better security for the settlers, who live or study in Hebron.
Mordechai said in an interview published on Friday that holding up the deal for more concessions from the Palestinians could risk igniting the whole region.

"Maybe we could have obtained more in one corner or another but that is the nature of negotiations. And today, because of some dump in Hebron we'll ignite the whole region?" Maariv newspaper quoted Mordechai as saying.
